chunk_findings.detail: The old line filtered the resolved decisions to those the state actually holds (`if d.id in st.decisions`) before subscripting `st.decisions[rec.id]`; the new code drops that guard and does `d = st.decisions[did]` for every id returned by `AB.decision_order(applied, ...)`. `applied` comes from `GI.for_item(...).applied`, and the only filter applied to it is `a.record.kind == "decision"` — nothing checks that the id is a key of `st.decisions`. The removed `if d.id in st.decisions` is direct evidence that `for_item(...)` can resolve a decision record that is not present in `st.decisions` (e.g. a record present in the guidance store but not loaded/superseded in state). Given such an item, `applied` yields that decision, `decision_order` puts its id in `ranked`, and line 29 raises `KeyError`, crashing `ddflow brief --for-agent` — whereas before the item rendered fine with that decision simply excluded. (`pins` are filtered with `if i in st.decisions`, but the ranked ids are not.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/briefing.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: `shown = max(cfg.session.agent_brief_decisions, len(cfg.session.agent_brief_pin_decisions))` uses the *configured* pin list length, while `_decision_lines` only keeps pins that satisfy `i in st.decisions`. The knob doc says unknown ids are ignored, so with a config such as `agent_brief_decisions = 2` and `agent_brief_pin_decisions = ["D-a", "D-b", "D-c", "D-typo"]` (none of them valid), `shown` becomes 4 instead of 2, and the brief quotes up to twice the decisions the knob permits — the exact "crowd out the relevant ones" behavior this change is meant to fix.

chunk_findings.detail: `pinned = sum(1 for i in cfg.session.agent_brief_pin_decisions if i in st.decisions)` counts every occurrence in the configured list, but the head that `_decision_lines` actually emits is deduplicated — `AB.decision_order` builds it with `dict.fromkeys(pins)` and `_decision_lines` renders that deduped head one line per id. The slice is therefore sized by a count that can exceed the number of pin lines, so the knob's cap breaks again. Given `agent_brief_decisions = 2` and `agent_brief_pin_decisions = ["D-a", "D-a", "D-b"]` with all three ids present in `st.decisions`, `pinned` becomes 3, `shown = max(2, 3) = 3`, and `facts.decisions[:3]` quotes D-a, D-b plus the top-ranked non-pinned decision — one more decision than the knob permits, which is exactly the crowding-out the change exists to prevent. Counting unique pinned ids (or slicing by `len(head)`) would keep the slice consistent with the emitted lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/briefing.py:94

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier review reported that the filter `if d.id in st.decisions` was dropped, so the code now does `d = st.decisions[did]` for every id yielded by `AB.decision_order(applied, ...)`, where `applied` comes from `GI.for_item(...).applied` and is only filtered on `a.record.kind == "decision"` — nothing guarantees the id is a key of `st.decisions`. That finding is still untriaged, and nothing visible in this change answers it: the new tests (`_decide` / `test_unknown_pinned_ids_do_not_widen_the_cap`) add every decision through `run_cli(..., "decision", "add", ...)`, which always populates `st.decisions`, so they never construct the failing input. Given a state in which an item carries an applied decision record whose id was never registered in `st.decisions` (e.g. an imported/pruned/orphaned decision id), `decision_order` returns that id and line 29 raises `KeyError` instead of the old code's silent skip — the brief crashes rather than omitting the unknown decision. None of the new assertions (glob ranking, pin ordering, cap widening) exercises or protects that path, so the defect stands.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/briefing.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: This is the previously reported, still-untriaged finding [2], and the visible part of the new change does not answer it. The candidate set handed to `AB.decision_order` is built from `GI.for_item(...).applied` filtered only on `a.record.kind == "decision"`; nothing in the change shown constrains those ids to keys of the repo's own store, yet the render loop then indexes `st.decisions[did]`. Given input where the global index surfaces an applicable decision whose id is not a key of `st.decisions` (an inherited/global decision, or an entry indexed from a store other than this repo's decision file) — say the brief is run as `ddflow brief --for-agent a T1 --phase P1` while the item's applied decisions include such an id — the lookup raises `KeyError` and the command dies with a traceback instead of emitting the brief. The newly added `test_unknown_pinned_ids_do_not_widen_the_cap` is not a probe for this: it only passes unknown ids through `session.agent_brief_pin_decisions` (the pin path), while every decision it creates with `_decide` exists in `st.decisions`, so the applied/unpinned path that does the unguarded lookup is never exercised. The finding therefore still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/briefing.py (the `d = st.decisions[did]` lookup after `AB.decision_order(applied, ...)`)
